board_events.latex: t_r = V_r - V_{r+1} \;\Rightarrow\; \sum_{r=1}^{n} t_r = V_1 - V_{n+1}

board_events.text: Like a relay: only the starting baton and the finish-line position matter.
For fractions, partial fractions produce the difference-form.
For products of integers, use the $V_n$ method; for surds, rationalise.
This is the tool for non-polynomial $t_n$ — where Unit 7's formulas fail.

segments.text: This final unit handles the sums that Unit seven cannot touch — where the general term is not a polynomial. The core idea is telescoping.
The picture says it all. A telescoping sum works like a collapsing telescope: each term cancels part of the next, so when you add everything, only the very first and very last pieces survive.
Formally, if you can write the r-th term as V-r minus V-r-plus-one, then the whole sum from one to n collapses to just V-one minus V-n-plus-one.
Think of a relay race where each runner hands off exactly what they received. Only the starting baton and the finish-line position matter; everything passed in between cancels in the bookkeeping.
The question is how to force a term into that difference-form. For a fraction, the tool is partial fractions.
For instance, one over r times r plus one splits cleanly into one over r minus one over r plus one — a perfect consecutive difference.
For products of consecutive integers, the tool is the V-n method — append a factor and divide. And for a surd in the denominator, you rationalise, which almost always produces a telescoper.
<curious> Keep the big picture: this unit is precisely the tool for non-polynomial general terms, exactly where Unit seven's standard-sum formulas break down.
यह आख़िरी unit उन sums को handle करता है जिन्हें Unit seven छू भी नहीं सकता — जहाँ general term एक polynomial नहीं है। core idea है telescoping।
picture सब कह देती है। एक telescoping sum एक collapsing telescope की तरह काम करती है: हर term अगले का हिस्सा cancel कर देता है, तो जब तुम सब कुछ add करते हो, सिर्फ़ पहला और आख़िरी piece बचता है।
formally, अगर तुम r-th term को V-r minus V-r-plus-one लिख सको, तो पूरा sum one से n तक बस V-one minus V-n-plus-one में collapse हो जाता है।
एक relay race सोचो जहाँ हर runner exactly वही pass करता है जो उसे मिला। सिर्फ़ starting baton और finish-line position matter करते हैं; बीच में pass हुआ सब कुछ bookkeeping में cancel हो जाता है।
सवाल है कि एक term को उस difference-form में कैसे force करें। एक fraction के लिए, tool है partial fractions।
उदाहरण के लिए, one over r times r plus one साफ़ split होता है one over r minus one over r plus one में — एक perfect consecutive difference।
consecutive integers के products के लिए, tool है V-n method — एक factor append करो और divide करो। और denominator में surd के लिए, तुम rationalise करते हो, जो लगभग हमेशा एक telescoper बना देता है।
<curious> big picture रखो: यह unit ठीक उन non-polynomial general terms का tool है, exactly वहाँ जहाँ Unit seven के standard-sum formulas टूट जाते हैं।

board_events.text: Partial fractions, the $V_n$ method, factorials, and surds
$V_n$ method: with $V_r = r(r+1)(r+2)$, we get $V_r - V_{r-1} = 3\,r(r+1)$.
Every derivation is the same shape: force a difference, then only ends survive.

segments.text: Let's build the standard telescopers, and notice they all share one shape.
First, the workhorse. One over r times r plus one splits into one over r minus one over r plus one, and summing collapses to one minus one over n plus one, which is n over n plus one.

For the triple product, one over r times r plus one times r plus two, split it as one half times the difference of one over r times r plus one and one over r plus one times r plus two. The bracket telescopes.
Now the V-n method for a product. Take V-r as r times r plus one times r plus two. Then V-r minus V-r-minus-one works out to three times r times r plus one.
So r times r plus one is one third of that difference, and the sum telescopes to one third of n times n plus one times n plus two.
For factorials, notice r times r-factorial equals r-plus-one-factorial minus r-factorial. Summing that telescopes cleanly to n-plus-one-factorial minus one.
And for surds, rationalising one over root r plus root r plus one gives root r plus one minus root r — a difference ready to collapse to root n plus one minus one.
<curious> Feel the common thread: every single derivation is the same move — force the term into a difference of consecutive things, and then only the endpoints survive.
चलो standard telescopers बनाएँ, और ध्यान दो कि ये सब एक ही shape share करते हैं।
पहले, workhorse। one over r times r plus one, one over r minus one over r plus one में split होता है, और sum करने पर one minus one over n plus one में collapse होता है, यानी n over n plus one।

triple product के लिए, one over r times r plus one times r plus two को one half times the difference of one over r times r plus one और one over r plus one times r plus two के रूप में split करो। bracket telescope करता है।
अब एक product के लिए V-n method। V-r को r times r plus one times r plus two लो। तब V-r minus V-r-minus-one निकलता है three times r times r plus one।
तो r times r plus one उस difference का one third है, और sum telescope होकर one third of n times n plus one times n plus two बनता है।
factorials के लिए, ध्यान दो r times r-factorial equals r-plus-one-factorial minus r-factorial। इसे sum करने पर साफ़ telescope होकर n-plus-one-factorial minus one बनता है।
और surds के लिए, one over root r plus root r plus one को rationalise करने पर root r plus one minus root r मिलता है — एक difference जो root n plus one minus one में collapse होने को तैयार है।
<curious> common thread महसूस करो: हर एक derivation वही move है — term को consecutive things के difference में force करो, और फिर सिर्फ़ endpoints बचते हैं।

board_events.text: The principle and the standard results

board_events.latex: t_r = V_r - V_{r+1} \;\Rightarrow\; \sum_{r=1}^{n} t_r = V_1 - V_{n+1}

board_events.text: Track the constant multiplier ($\tfrac12$, $\tfrac1k$) — dropping it is a classic slip.

segments.text: Let's consolidate the telescoping toolkit — the principle first, then the standard results worth recognising on sight.
The principle is the whole unit in one line: if the r-th term is V-r minus V-r-plus-one, the sum is simply V-one minus V-n-plus-one.
The first standard result: the sum of one over r times r plus one is n over n plus one.
The triple-product sum is n times n plus three, over four times n plus one times n plus two.
For the odd-factor product, the sum of one over two r minus one times two r plus one is n over two n plus one.
The V-n method generalises the whole family: the sum of a product of k consecutive integers is the product of k plus one consecutive integers, divided by k plus one.
And two more to keep close: the sum of r times r-factorial is n-plus-one-factorial minus one, and the surd sum is root n plus one minus one.

<whisper> One warning that catches people out: track the constant multiplier. The triple product carries a one half, the odd-factor split carries a one half too — dropping that constant is a classic, silent slip.
चलो telescoping toolkit consolidate करें — पहले principle, फिर standard results जो देखते ही पहचानने लायक हैं।
principle पूरा unit एक line में है: अगर r-th term V-r minus V-r-plus-one हो, तो sum बस V-one minus V-n-plus-one है।
पहला standard result: one over r times r plus one का sum है n over n plus one।
triple-product sum है n times n plus three, over four times n plus one times n plus two।
odd-factor product के लिए, one over two r minus one times two r plus one का sum है n over two n plus one।
V-n method पूरे family को generalise करता है: k consecutive integers के product का sum, k plus one consecutive integers का product है, k plus one से divided।
और दो और पास रखो: r times r-factorial का sum है n-plus-one-factorial minus one, और surd sum है root n plus one minus one।
<whisper> एक warning जो लोगों को पकड़ती है: constant multiplier track करो। triple product एक one half रखता है, odd-factor split भी एक one half — उस constant को गिरा देना एक classic, silent slip है।

sections.title: The basic telescoper and its infinite limit

board_events.text: Find Σ 1/[r(r+1)] to n terms, and its value as n → ∞
Every interior term appears once with $+$ and once with $-$.

segments.text: Let's open the telescoping examples with the cleanest case — the sum of one over r times r plus one, and what it approaches as n grows.
The first move is partial fractions: one over r times r plus one splits into one over r minus one over r plus one.
Now write out the sum term by term: one minus one half, plus one half minus one third, and so on to one over n minus one over n plus one.
Look at what happens. Every interior fraction appears once with a plus and once with a minus, so they annihilate in pairs.
Only the outermost survivors remain: the leading one, and the trailing minus one over n plus one. So the sum is one minus one over n plus one, which is n over n plus one.
As n grows without bound, that trailing fraction vanishes and the sum approaches one.
<excited> So the infinite series one over one-times-two, plus one over two-times-three, and onward, equals exactly one — a beautifully clean result straight out of the collapse.
चलो telescoping examples को सबसे clean case से खोलें — one over r times r plus one का sum, और यह n बढ़ने पर किसकी तरफ़ जाता है।
पहला move है partial fractions: one over r times r plus one, one over r minus one over r plus one में split होता है।
अब sum को term by term लिखो: one minus one half, plus one half minus one third, और ऐसे ही one over n minus one over n plus one तक।
देखो क्या होता है। हर interior fraction एक बार plus के साथ और एक बार minus के साथ आता है, तो वे pairs में एक-दूसरे को खत्म कर देते हैं।
सिर्फ़ बाहरी survivors बचते हैं: शुरू का one, और आख़िरी minus one over n plus one। तो sum है one minus one over n plus one, यानी n over n plus one।
जैसे-जैसे n बिना सीमा बढ़ता है, वो आख़िरी fraction गायब हो जाता है और sum one की तरफ़ पहुँचता है।
<excited> तो infinite series one over one-times-two, plus one over two-times-three, और आगे, exactly one के बराबर है — collapse से सीधे निकला एक खूबसूरत clean result।

sections.title: A partial-fraction telescoper with a step of 3

board_events.text: The factors step by 3: general term is $\tfrac{1}{(3r-2)(3r+1)}$.
The bracket telescopes; the $\tfrac13$ rides along outside.
Keep the $\tfrac13$ from the split — losing it is the telescope-lost-multiplier trap.

segments.text: This example is the same idea with a twist — the denominators step by three instead of one, and a constant multiplier appears.
Read the pattern in the denominators: one and four, four and seven, seven and ten. So the r-th term is one over three r minus two, times three r plus one.
Partial fractions split this, but watch the constant: it becomes one third times the difference of one over three r minus two and one over three r plus one.
The bracket telescopes exactly as before, while the one third simply rides along on the outside of the whole sum.
After the interior terms cancel, we're left with one third times the quantity one minus one over three n plus one.
Simplifying, that is n over three n plus one.

<whisper> The one thing to guard here is that factor of one third from the split. Forgetting it gives a plausible-looking answer that's wrong by a factor of three — the telescope-lost-multiplier trap.
यह example वही idea है एक twist के साथ — denominators one के बजाय three से step करते हैं, और एक constant multiplier आता है।
denominators में pattern पढ़ो: one और four, four और seven, seven और ten। तो r-th term है one over three r minus two, times three r plus one।
partial fractions इसे split करते हैं, पर constant देखो: यह बनता है one third times the difference of one over three r minus two और one over three r plus one।
bracket exactly पहले जैसा telescope करता है, जबकि one third बस पूरे sum के बाहर साथ चलता है।
interior terms cancel होने के बाद, हमारे पास बचता है one third times the quantity one minus one over three n plus one।
simplify करने पर, यह है n over three n plus one।
<whisper> यहाँ guard करने वाली एक चीज़ है split से आया वो one third factor। इसे भूलना एक plausible दिखने वाला answer देता है जो three के factor से गलत है — telescope-lost-multiplier trap।

sections.title: The Vₙ method on a product of three

board_events.text: Find Σ r(r+1)(r+2) from r = 1 to n
A product of 3 consecutive integers — use the $V_n$ method.
Here $k = 3$: append one more factor, divide by $k + 1 = 4$.
Divide by (number of factors + 1) — the $V_n$-method-divisor rule.

segments.text: This example shows the V-n method at its cleanest, on a product of three consecutive integers.
Rather than expand into a cubic and sum term by term, we use the V-n shortcut, which mirrors how integration raises a power.
The general rule: the sum of a product of k consecutive integers equals the product of k plus one consecutive integers, divided by k plus one.
Here k is three. So we append one more factor — n plus three — and divide by k plus one, which is four.
That gives the sum directly as n times n plus one times n plus two times n plus three, over four.
Verify with n equals one: the sum should be one times two times three, which is six, and the formula gives one times two times three times four over four, also six. It checks.
<curious> The one rule to lock in is the divisor: you divide by the number of factors plus one. Using the wrong divisor is the classic V-n-method slip.
यह example V-n method को उसके सबसे clean रूप में दिखाता है, तीन consecutive integers के एक product पर।
एक cubic में expand करके term by term sum करने के बजाय, हम V-n shortcut use करते हैं, जो mirror करता है कि integration एक power कैसे बढ़ाता है।
general rule: k consecutive integers के product का sum, k plus one consecutive integers के product के बराबर है, k plus one से divided।
यहाँ k three है। तो हम एक और factor append करते हैं — n plus three — और k plus one, यानी four से divide करते हैं।
इससे sum सीधे मिलता है n times n plus one times n plus two times n plus three, over four।
n equals one से verify करो: sum one times two times three, यानी six होना चाहिए, और formula देता है one times two times three times four over four, भी six। यह check हो गया।
<curious> lock करने वाला एक rule है divisor: तुम number of factors plus one से divide करते हो। गलत divisor use करना classic V-n-method slip है।

board_events.text: Evaluate Σ r/(r+1)! from r = 1 to n
Rewrite the numerator: $r = (r+1) - 1$.
This is a difference of consecutive reciprocal factorials.
Look for $t_r = f(r) - f(r+1)$ with $f$ a factorial expression.

segments.text: This example telescopes a factorial series with a small but clever rewrite of the numerator.
The trick is to split the numerator. Write r as r plus one, minus one — a harmless-looking move that unlocks everything.
Now r over r-plus-one-factorial becomes r plus one minus one, over r-plus-one-factorial, which separates into one over r-factorial minus one over r-plus-one-factorial.
And that is exactly a difference of consecutive reciprocal factorials — a telescoper in disguise.
Summing, all the interior terms cancel, leaving one over one-factorial minus one over n-plus-one-factorial, which is one minus one over n-plus-one-factorial.
As n grows, the trailing factorial term races to zero, so the infinite sum is exactly one.

<curious> The habit worth carrying: for factorial sums, look for a way to write the term as f of r minus f of r plus one, where f is some factorial expression. Once you spot it, the collapse is automatic.
यह example एक factorial series को telescope करता है, numerator के एक छोटे पर clever rewrite के साथ।
trick है numerator को split करना। r को r plus one, minus one लिखो — एक harmless दिखने वाला move जो सब कुछ unlock कर देता है।
अब r over r-plus-one-factorial बन जाता है r plus one minus one, over r-plus-one-factorial, जो separate होता है one over r-factorial minus one over r-plus-one-factorial में।
और यह exactly consecutive reciprocal factorials का एक difference है — disguise में एक telescoper।
sum करने पर, सारे interior terms cancel हो जाते हैं, बचता है one over one-factorial minus one over n-plus-one-factorial, यानी one minus one over n-plus-one-factorial।
जैसे-जैसे n बढ़ता है, आख़िरी factorial term zero की ओर दौड़ता है, तो infinite sum exactly one है।
<curious> ले जाने लायक habit: factorial sums के लिए, term को f of r minus f of r plus one लिखने का तरीका ढूँढो, जहाँ f कोई factorial expression हो। जैसे ही spot करो, collapse automatic है।

sections.title: A surd telescoper, evaluated at n = 99

board_events.text: Sum Σ 1/(√r + √(r+1)), then evaluate for n = 99
Rationalise the denominator to unlock the difference-form.
Rationalising turns a sum of awkward fractions into a clean telescoper.

segments.text: This Advanced example telescopes a surd series, and the key move is rationalising the denominator.
Each term looks intimidating — one over root r plus root r plus one — but rationalising tames it completely.
Multiply top and bottom by root r plus one minus root r. The denominator becomes a difference of squares: root r plus one squared minus root r squared, which is just one.
So each term collapses to simply root r plus one minus root r — a clean consecutive difference.
Summing telescopes it: everything cancels except the endpoints, leaving root n plus one minus one.
Now evaluate at n equals ninety-nine: root of one hundred minus one, which is ten minus one, equal to nine.
<excited> That is the whole payoff — rationalising converted a sum of awkward-looking fractions into a clean telescoper, and a hundred-term sum came down to a single, tidy nine.
यह Advanced example एक surd series को telescope करता है, और key move है denominator को rationalise करना।
हर term डरावना दिखता है — one over root r plus root r plus one — पर rationalising इसे पूरी तरह वश में कर लेता है।
ऊपर-नीचे को root r plus one minus root r से multiply करो। denominator बन जाता है difference of squares: root r plus one squared minus root r squared, यानी बस one।
तो हर term बस root r plus one minus root r में collapse होता है — एक clean consecutive difference।
sum करने पर यह telescope होता है: endpoints के अलावा सब cancel, बचता है root n plus one minus one।
अब n equals ninety-nine पर evaluate करो: root of one hundred minus one, यानी ten minus one, बराबर nine।
<excited> यही पूरा payoff है — rationalising ने awkward दिखने वाली fractions के sum को एक clean telescoper में बदल दिया, और सौ-term का sum एक अकेले, tidy nine पर आ गया।

sections.title: Telescoping: the traps and the pro-tips

board_events.text: Telescoping — the traps, and the fast moves
No difference-form: brute-forcing or applying $\sum n^k$ to a fraction/surd.
Endpoint sign: the answer is $V_1 - V_{n+1}$, not $V_0 - V_n$ — watch off-by-one.
Lost multiplier: keep the $\tfrac12$ or $\tfrac1k$ the split carries.
$V_n$ divisor: divide by (number of factors + 1).
Pro-tip: fraction → partial fractions; product → $V_n$; surd → rationalise.
Factorials → write $t_r = f(r+1) - f(r)$.
After telescoping, the answer is always (first survivor) − (last survivor).

segments.text: Let's close Unit eight with the telescoping traps and the fast moves that beat them.
The dominant error is failing to reach a difference-form at all — brute-forcing the sum, or trying to apply the polynomial standard-sum formulas to a fraction or a surd, where they simply don't fit.
Second is the endpoint sign. After collapse, the answer is V-one minus V-n-plus-one — not V-nought minus V-n. Off-by-one on the surviving endpoints is the main slip.
Third, don't lose the multiplier. When the split carries a one half or a one over k, that constant must ride all the way through to the final answer.
Fourth, in the V-n method, divide by the number of factors plus one — the wrong divisor quietly wrecks the result.

<curious> Now the decision tree. For a fraction, try partial fractions and look for a consecutive-shift difference. For a product of consecutive terms, use the V-n method. For a surd in the denominator, rationalise.
And for factorials, hunt for a way to write the term as f of r plus one minus f of r, with f a factorial expression.
Above all, remember the shape of every telescoping answer: it is always the first surviving term minus the last surviving term. If your answer isn't in that form, you haven't finished collapsing.
चलो Unit eight को telescoping traps और उन्हें हराने वाले fast moves के साथ बंद करें।
dominant error है difference-form तक पहुँच ही न पाना — sum को brute-force करना, या एक fraction या surd पर polynomial standard-sum formulas apply करने की कोशिश करना, जहाँ वे fit ही नहीं होते।
दूसरा है endpoint sign। collapse के बाद, answer है V-one minus V-n-plus-one — V-nought minus V-n नहीं। surviving endpoints पर off-by-one main slip है।
तीसरा, multiplier मत खोओ। जब split एक one half या one over k रखे, वो constant final answer तक पूरे रास्ते साथ चलना चाहिए।
चौथा, V-n method में, number of factors plus one से divide करो — गलत divisor चुपके से result बर्बाद कर देता है।

<curious> अब decision tree। एक fraction के लिए, partial fractions try करो और एक consecutive-shift difference ढूँढो। consecutive terms के product के लिए, V-n method use करो। denominator में surd के लिए, rationalise करो।
और factorials के लिए, term को f of r plus one minus f of r लिखने का तरीका ढूँढो, f एक factorial expression के साथ।
सबसे ऊपर, हर telescoping answer का shape याद रखो: यह हमेशा first surviving term minus last surviving term है। अगर तुम्हारा answer उस form में नहीं, तो तुमने collapse पूरा नहीं किया।

segments.text: Here is your complete toolkit for the whole chapter, gathered on a single board. This is a recap — we're restating, not re-teaching, so let the formulas trigger the reasoning you already know.
Arithmetic progressions: the n-th term is a plus n minus one d, and the sum is n over two times two a plus n minus one d, or equivalently n over two times a plus last term.

Geometric progressions: the n-th term is a r to the n minus one, the finite sum is a times one minus r to the n over one minus r, and the sum to infinity is a over one minus r when the size of r is below one.
Harmonic progressions: reciprocate to an AP, the harmonic mean is two a b over a plus b, and remember the p-th-equals-q result, n-th term equals p q over n.
The means relationship: arithmetic at least geometric at least harmonic, the identity A H equals G squared, and recovery of the numbers as A plus or minus the root of A squared minus G squared.
Arithmetico-geometric progressions: the general term is a plus n minus one d, times r to the n minus one, with the compact sum to infinity a over one minus r plus d r over one minus r squared.
The special sums: the sum of r, the sum of r squared, and the memorable sum of cubes equals the square of the sum.
And telescoping: t-r equals V-r minus V-r-plus-one collapses to V-one minus V-n-plus-one, with the flagship sum of one over r times r plus one equal to n over n plus one.
<excited> That single board is everything the chapter rests on — carry it into the exam hall and every problem becomes a matter of choosing the right tool.

board_events.text: Fast recall: one line per idea
AP: $a_n = a + (n-1)d$; test — $a_n$ linear, or $S_n$ quadratic with zero constant.
GP: $a_n = a r^{n-1}$; $S_\infty$ needs $|r| < 1$; for '$a,b,c$ in GP' use $b^2 = ac$.
HP: reciprocate → AP; $H = \tfrac{2ab}{a+b}$; no general sum formula.
Means: $A \ge G \ge H$; $AH = G^2$; recover via $x^2 - 2Ax + G^2 = 0$.
AGP: multiply by $r$, shift, subtract; $S_\infty = \tfrac{a}{1-r} + \tfrac{dr}{(1-r)^2}$.
Special sums: find $t_n$ → powers of $n$ → apply; shortcut $\sum n^3 = (\sum n)^2$.
Telescope: write $t_r$ as a difference; only $V_1 - V_{n+1}$ survives.
Golden habit throughout: position → general term $a_n$ → then list or sum.

segments.text: Finally, the quick-recall cheat sheet — one line per idea, the kind of thing to skim minutes before an exam.
For arithmetic progressions: the n-th term is a plus n minus one d, and to test whether something is an AP, check that the term is linear in n, or that the sum is quadratic with a zero constant.
For geometric progressions: the n-th term is a r to the n minus one, the infinite sum needs the size of r below one, and for any three-in-GP condition reach straight for b squared equals a c.
For harmonic progressions: reciprocate to an AP, the harmonic mean is two a b over a plus b, and remember there is no general sum formula.
For the means: arithmetic at least geometric at least harmonic, the identity A H equals G squared, and recover two numbers from the quadratic x squared minus two A x plus G squared.
For arithmetico-geometric progressions: multiply the sum by r, shift, and subtract; and the compact infinite sum is a over one minus r plus d r over one minus r squared.
For special sums: find the general term, express it in powers of n, and apply the standard sums, with the shortcut that the sum of cubes is the square of the sum.
For telescoping: write the term as a difference of consecutive things, and only the first and last survivors remain.

<whisper> And carry the golden habit through everything: go from position, to the general term a sub n, and only then decide whether to list or to sum. Get that reflex right and the whole chapter is yours.
